thesis: BILL Holdings fell about 4.1% to $61.45 (from $64.08) on 14.3x volume after agreeing on Nov 19 to be taken private by TPG, with Corpay taking a minority stake, for $63.25 per share in cash (company DEFA14A filing), a 31% premium to the 60-day VWAP ending Nov 16. Closing is expected in 1H 2027, subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals, with no financing condition. The shares had traded above the deal price on Financial Times reports of the talks ($66.01 close on Nov 18); today's slide back below $63.25 suggests the market now prices the agreed cash price rather than a higher bid. With the price fixed, the remaining upside is a ~2.9% spread over several months, while a broken deal would leave the shares exposed to their pre-report level (about $4.8B market value before the reports). The strongest plausible positive, a competing bid, isn't ruled out (Elliott, Starboard and Barington had pushed for a sale), but no rival offer was found. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation over the deal and no restatement. Medium; avoid.
invalidation: A competing proposal above $63.25 emerges, or the merger agreement is terminated.
sources: Payments Dive (Bill sells for $6B to TPG, Corpay): https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/bill-sells-for-6b-to-tpg-corpay/875331/

thesis: Brookfield Infrastructure Corp rose about 4.9% to $43.09 (from $41.08) on 5.0x volume, the day after its corporate simplification closed: on Nov 19 the court-approved arrangement combined BIP and BIPC into BIP Inc., holders received Class A shares one-for-one, and the NYSE/TSX symbol is set to become "BIP" on Nov 23, 2026 (company release). BIP Inc. also declared a $0.455 quarterly dividend (record Nov 30, payable Dec 31) and took over BIP's buyback; Q3 FFO, reported Nov 6, rose 10% to $717M. This run found no other company news for today, which suggests the volume and price jump reflect exchange and index mechanics around the combination rather than a new operating result. The litigation check found a long-running Peru toll-road discovery dispute naming Brookfield Infrastructure Partners with no scheduled ruling found, and an unverified blog claim of an SEC probe; no restatement. A structure-driven move makes this low, and the BIPC symbol is retired on Nov 23; avoid.
invalidation: Trading under the new BIP symbol settles and a company-disclosed result or guidance drives the shares.
sources: Yahoo Finance (company release, completion of corporate simplification): https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/brookfield-infrastructure-announces-completion-corporate-120000633.html

thesis: Elastic fell about 8.0% on Nov 19 (to $76.33 from $83.01) after its fiscal Q2 2027 report and another 1.5% today to $75.17 on 3.5x volume. The quarter beat: revenue of $496M rose 17%, sales-led subscription revenue rose 19% to $415M, cRPO grew 19% (20% in constant currency), non-GAAP operating margin hit a record 22.2%, and full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised to $3.35-3.41. But the full-year revenue midpoint stayed at $2.004B because a $9.5M FX cut offset the Q2 beat, and Q3 revenue guidance of $507.5-508.5M sits below the ~$518M pre-report consensus Benzinga listed. A beat offset by a below-consensus next-quarter guide makes the evidence mixed. The litigation check found the 2024 securities class action in the Eastern District of New York with no current status or scheduled step found, and July 2026 Pomerantz investigation notices with no filed complaint; no restatement. Low; avoid.
invalidation: Q3 results beat the guide and growth re-accelerates, so the shares recover above the pre-report close (~$83.01).
sources: Investing.com (Q2 FY27 slides, stock slides on concerns): https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/elastic-q2-fy27-slides-record-margins-amid-ai-growth-stock-slides-on-concerns-93CH-4994607

thesis: BJ's Wholesale fell about 5.2% to $104.96 (from $110.75) on 3.3x volume after its fiscal Q3 2026 report on Nov 20 (8-K): adjusted EPS of $1.73 beat the $1.26 consensus, comparable club sales rose 4.1% excluding gasoline (13.5% including), membership fee income rose 9.5% to $138.4M, and full-year guidance was raised (comparable sales ex-gas to at least 2.5% from 2%, adjusted EPS to $5.10-5.30 from $4.60-4.80). Offsetting that, coverage reports the quarter included an approximately $145M pretax benefit from a litigation settlement (the interchange-fee settlement disclosed in a Sept 4 8-K), merchandise gross margin contracted, and management gave no 2027 guidance. A beat and raise flattered by a one-time gain, with margin pressure, makes the evidence mixed. The litigation check found the settled interchange-fee case with no scheduled step remaining, and no investigation or restatement. Low.
invalidation: Merchandise margins keep contracting, the raised EPS guide proves mostly one-time, or ex-gas comparable sales slow below the 2.5% floor.
sources: Benzinga (falls despite beat, one-time gain boosts profit): https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/11/63468510/bjs-wholesale-stock-falls-despite-q3-earnings-beat-raised-outlook-as-one-time-gain-boosts-profit

thesis: APi Group rose about 0.6% to $42.11 (from $41.86) on 2.9x volume, holding just above its 200-day average (~$42.01); this run found no company news dated today beyond the Nov 17 pricing of EUR 500M of 5.25% senior notes due 2032 to repay revolver borrowings (closing expected by Nov 30), which is debt, not equity. The thesis rests on the Oct 29 Q3 2026 release: record net revenue of about $2.6B, up 22.5% (15.7% organic), net income up 22.6% to $114M, adjusted EBITDA up 24.6% to $350M with margin up 20bp to 13.7%, and full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges raised for the third time this year. The strongest counter-case is balance-sheet and cash quality: net leverage rose to 2.4x from 1.6x on acquisitions, free-cash-flow conversion guidance was trimmed to about 110% from 115%, the implied full-year EBITDA margin drifted to 13.5% from 13.8%, and a director sold 287,498 shares on Nov 9. Even so, 15.7% organic growth shows the gains aren't only acquired, and cash conversion still above 100% suggests the leverage is being serviced from operations, so the net read stays positive. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. The report is 16 trading days old, past the 15-day window for a fresh-money high. Medium.
invalidation: Organic growth slows sharply or the raised outlook is cut, leverage keeps rising without matching EBITDA, or the shares close back below the 200-day average.

thesis: Global Payments jumped about 10.0% to $91.84 (from $83.52) on 2.5x volume after a Bloomberg report that GTCR, its largest holder with about 16%, is working with other buyout firms on a possible deal valued around $50B including debt; a Reuters-cited report put it near $40B of enterprise value with Clayton, Dubilier & Rice involved and talks at an early stage, and coverage says earlier talks had been halted. The shares were briefly halted for volatility and touched $95.50. No company disclosure confirms any approach, and the stock set a 52-week high of $102.905 on Nov 10 before sliding to $83.52 by Nov 19. The litigation check found only the Active Network securities suit, settled for $3.6M with final judgment in December 2024, and no investigation or restatement. A move driven by an unconfirmed takeover report, after earlier talks stalled, is rumor-driven; low, avoid.
invalidation: The company confirms an approach or signs a definitive agreement (the shares then trade to the deal terms), or talks end and a company-disclosed result drives the shares.

thesis: AES was flat at $15.02 on 2.4x volume, just above the $15.00 per-share cash price in its pending take-private by a Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) and EQT-led consortium. On Nov 17 the company disclosed (8-K) the final FERC order, the last suspensory regulatory approval, and coverage puts the expected closing at Dec 2, 2026, after which the shares stop trading on the NYSE; stockholders approved the deal on June 26 with about 98% of votes cast. The strongest plausible positive, a raised price, doesn't change the read: the consideration is fixed by a stockholder-approved agreement with all suspensory approvals received, and the shares already trade at or above $15.00, leaving no upside to capture before delisting. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation against the deal and no restatement. High; avoid.
invalidation: The closing is delayed or the agreement is terminated, or the consideration is changed.

thesis: Synaptics slipped about 1.0% to $115.75 (from $116.91) on 2.5x volume. On Nov 17 stockholders approved the amended (Oct 1, 2026) merger agreement under which onsemi acquires the company (8-K: 31.2M votes for, 0.5M against), with closing expected in mid-2027 subject to regulatory clearances. Sources this run found disagree on the consideration: the proxy lists $123.00 per share in cash, while the annual report describes 1.350 onsemi shares per share. So the remaining spread to the deal value can't be pinned down, and no report on antitrust clearance status was found. The shares now trade on deal terms and a regulatory outcome rather than Synaptics' own results, and with the consideration unresolved in this run's sources the evidence is unresolved. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation and no restatement. Low; avoid.
invalidation: Regulators clear the deal and the consideration is confirmed (the shares then trade to it), or the agreement is terminated.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22 on the Oct 21 proposal). ROIV slipped about 0.8% to $38.65 (from $38.96), about 9.1% below its 52-week high and above the $37.64 cost; this run found no company disclosure dated after the Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release. That release reported $31.0M of LISRAYA (brepocitinib) net product revenue in its first five weeks after the Aug 27 FDA approval in dermatomyositis, and a plan to file an sNDA in non-infectious uveitis in 1H calendar 2027 after the Oct 21 Phase 3 wins; an Investor Day is set for Dec 9. The counter-case named in the prior thesis stays open: the uveitis data are not an approval, the sNDA is still months away, and the batoclimab thyroid-eye-disease Phase 3 miss shows pipeline risk. The litigation check found the March 2026 Moderna LNP settlement (up to $2.25B: $950M paid, up to $1.3B more contingent on a Federal Circuit appeal of the government-contractor defense, with no argument or ruling date found) and the Pfizer/BioNTech suit with no trial date; no restatement. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or the Federal Circuit rules for Moderna and removes the contingent payment.

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed Nov 9). NWL fell about 1.9% to $5.305 (from $5.41), about 8.8% below the $5.82 cost, and MarketBeat noted it crossed below its 50-day average. Company disclosures since the opening buy are routine: the Nov 4 declaration of the regular $0.07 quarterly dividend (record Nov 30) and the Nov 9 election of Bill Newlands to the board effective Jan 1, 2027. Analyst moves were mixed: Citi cut its target to $5.50 and UBS raised to $5.75, both neutral, and Zacks cut to hold. The entry thesis rested on the Oct 30 Q3 report, which topped the company's sales guidance and raised its full-year net sales outlook, and the counter-cases named in the prior thesis stay open: the operating cash flow outlook was cut about 62% to $150M, with about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment. Time review: 13 trading days after the opening buy, the peak gain is +5.5% (high $6.14), short of the +8% first tier, and neither post-entry disclosure is a fact that supports the holding thesis, so the direction is exit_existing. The litigation check found only the 2023 SEC settlement over non-GAAP core sales, whose fair-fund distribution plan was amended by an SEC order on Oct 29, 2026, and no new investigation or restatement. Low.
invalidation: A new company-disclosed fact that changes the cash-flow outlook, such as raised operating cash flow guidance or a refinancing on better terms.

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 19 on the Nov 18 proposal). H World edged up about 0.1% to $51.08 (from $51.01), about 1.9% below the $52.06 fill and 9.8% below its 52-week high; this run found no company disclosure dated after the Nov 16 Q3 2026 report. That report (company release) showed revenue up 11.3% to about RMB 7.8B, ahead of the ~RMB 7.33B consensus, net income attributable of RMB 1.8B, and 2026 group revenue growth guidance raised to 9-10% from 4-8%. The counter-case named in the prior thesis stays open: same-hotel RevPAR fell 4.4%, and one report flags the dollar revenue range as below consensus, so the raised guide isn't a clean beat.
